review_output: {"summary":"Narrow follow-up review of the projection revision trigger (20261015200000) and the guard-error mapping in publishRegistrationCoverage. The append-only ledger trigger does fix the earlier HIGH concern for row-level INSERT and DELETE on LiveMetricRegistration. Deleting a projection adds a ledger event, the reader then drops proofs whose stored registration revision no longer matches the live count, and the vendor-cascade skip (Vendor row no longer visible) is consistent with the immutable-ledger delete exception. I found no BLOCKER in the changed code. Remaining gaps: (1) on UPDATE, the trigger only writes an event for the NEW (vendorId, liveId), so a registration moved to another live never invalidates the old live's proofs, unless an immutability guard I can't see blocks such updates; (2) TRUNCATE skips row triggers and this migration adds no no-truncate guard on LiveMetricRegistration, so the projection can be emptied while old proofs still validate; (3) the guard-error mapping depends on the shared SQLSTATE 23514 plus a message substring and the Prisma meta shape, and no supplied test exercises it (it fails safe: an error instead of source_changed); (4) deleting only a Live leaves ledger rows that can never be deleted, and the trigger can append more of them during a Live cascade. The earlier open findings (O(n) counts, broad live revision liveness, full lifecycle interleavings, app least-privilege role) stay open and are not repeated here. This is not full acceptance.","findings":[{"area":"Projection revision fence / UPDATE path","file":"prisma/migrations/20261015200000_live_metric_registration_projection_revision/migration.sql","issue":"On UPDATE, the trigger only writes an event for NEW.vendorId and NEW.liveId (line 7: fact:=NEW). If an UPDATE moves a registration to a different live, or to a version under a different live, the OLD scope gets no ledger event and its revision count does not change.","evidence":"Line 7: IF TG_OP='DELETE' THEN fact:=OLD; ELSE fact:=NEW; END IF; then a single INSERT for fact's scope. Nothing emits an event for OLD when (OLD.vendorId, OLD.liveId) differs from NEW. The supplied probes only test duplicate INSERT and DELETE, not a scope-changing UPDATE.","impact":"A covered proof for the old live keeps passing the reader's check (registrationRevision = current count) even though one of its matched projections has moved away. The report would show stale 'complete' coverage, which is the kind of false-positive the fence is meant to prevent. This only applies if LiveMetricRegistration updates are allowed; I can't see an immutability guard in the supplied text.","recommended_fix":"For UPDATE, emit an event for OLD's scope and also for NEW's scope when it differs, in a fixed order. Alternatively, add a BEFORE UPDATE trigger that rejects changes to vendorId, liveId, versionId, submissionId and verifiedAt with 23514, so this case cannot happen.","required_test":"In a rolled-back transaction, update a matched registration to another live, or to another version on another live, if FKs allow it. Assert either that the update is rejected with 23514, or that wp20_metric_registration_revision rises for the old scope and a fresh report for the old scope returns unknown.","confidence":0.5,"severity":"MAJOR"},{"area":"Projection revision fence / TRUNCATE bypass","file":"prisma/migrations/20261015200000_live_metric_registration_projection_revision/migration.sql","issue":"The new trigger is FOR EACH ROW only. TRUNCATE on LiveMetricRegistration, or TRUNCATE ... CASCADE from a table it references, removes every projection without firing row triggers. This migration adds no BEFORE TRUNCATE guard on LiveMetricRegistration.","evidence":"Lines 16-17 create AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ... FOR EACH ROW only. The ledger and capture tables both have no-truncate triggers (170000 lines 37-38, 100000 lines 40-41), but the supplied text has none for LiveMetricRegistration. The reported TRUNCATE test targets the source table and is blocked by the capture table, not the projection table.","impact":"Existing 'covered' registration proofs would still match the unchanged ledger count after the projection table is emptied, so coverage would be reported as complete while there are no projections behind it. It needs a role with TRUNCATE, but the app least-privilege-role finding is still open.","recommended_fix":"Add a BEFORE TRUNCATE FOR EACH STATEMENT trigger on LiveMetricRegistration that raises 23514, reusing a no-truncate function. Revoke TRUNCATE from the app and API roles.","required_test":"Probe: TRUNCATE \"LiveMetricRegistration\" and TRUNCATE \"LiveMetricRegistration\" CASCADE inside a savepoint must both fail with 23514. Also assert that a fresh report after the attempt is still complete with the original proof.","confidence":0.6,"severity":"MAJOR"},{"area":"Guard-error mapping","file":"src/lib/live-metric-registration-coverage.ts","issue":"The mapping to source_changed depends on Prisma returning P2010 with meta.code '23514' and a meta.message containing the guard text. 23514 is also used by the registrationRevision/registrationCount CHECK constraints and by other guards. The meta shape differs between engine and driver-adapter setups, and no supplied test drives the guard through publishRegistrationCoverage.","evidence":"Lines 37-40 match on error.code==='P2010' && meta.code==='23514' && meta.message.includes('registration coverage source mismatch'). The mutation and cascade scripts never call publishRegistrationCoverage while a source change commits between line 25 and the INSERT on line 27.","impact":"It fails safe: if the mapping doesn't match, the error is re-thrown, no stale proof is written, and the reader also re-checks the revision. But the race that this code exists for has no test, and a change to the Prisma or adapter error shape would silently turn source_changed into a 500.","recommended_fix":"Give the guard its own SQLSTATE (for example a custom P0-class code) and match on code only, or put the error matching in a tested helper. Keep the explicit pre-read on lines 24-26.","required_test":"A deterministic test that inserts a registrations/covered audit through tx.$queryRaw with a stale registrationRevision and asserts the helper returns source_changed. Also an integration test where a second connection commits a VERIFIED FormSubmission change between the revision read and the INSERT (for example via an advisory-lock barrier); it should return source_changed and write no row.","confidence":0.55,"severity":"MINOR"},{"area":"Ledger lifecycle on Live-only deletion","file":"prisma/migrations/20261015200000_live_metric_registration_projection_revision/migration.sql","issue":"The trigger skips an event only when the Vendor or the matching LiveMetricVersion is gone. When a Live is deleted while its Vendor remains, events can still be written for the deleted live if the registration is deleted (for example via the FormSubmission cascade) while the version is still visible. Ledger rows only have an FK to Vendor, and the immutable trigger refuses DELETE while the Vendor exists, so these rows can never be removed.","evidence":"Lines 9-12 check only the Vendor and the version. LiveMetricRegistrationSource has an FK on vendorId only (170000 line 5). wp20_metric_registration_source_immutable only allows DELETE when the Vendor row is missing (170000 line 32). The supplied cascade test covers Vendor deletion only.","impact":"Ledger rows for deleted Lives build up permanently and can't be cleaned up without disabling triggers, which also adds to the open O(n) count concern. It does not create false coverage, because audits for a deleted live can't be reached through the version join.","recommended_fix":"Also skip the INSERT when the Live row is no longer visible. Either add an FK from LiveMetricRegistrationSource(liveId) to Live ON DELETE CASCADE and extend the immutable exception to allow deletion when the Live is gone, or document the retention behaviour and add a sweep job.","required_test":"Seed a live with a verified submission, its projection, a report and a proof, then delete only the Live. Assert the Vendor remains, there are no capture, registration or report orphans, and LiveMetricRegistrationSource has no rows left for that liveId (or that the documented retained count matches).","confidence":0.45,"severity":"MINOR"}]}
